questions.heading: Element Reads a List at a Variable Index
questions.stem: A job's method is an integer variable m in {0, 1, 2}, and the list W = [5, 3, 2] gives its weeks by method. Which call makes the variable weeks equal to the entry of W at position m?

options.says: The first argument is the index and the last the target; this reads W at position weeks and stores it in m.
That only restricts m to the values 5, 3 and 2; it never mentions weeks.
Right: add_element(index, expressions, target) sets target = expressions[index].
add_max_equality sets the target to the largest entry, 5, whatever the method.

questions.heading: A Table Lists Every Combination That Is Allowed
questions.stem: The own crew offers manual work at $30k and mechanical at $40k; a contractor offers mechanical at $55k and aerial at $70k. A modeler writes two tables, allowed (method, who) pairs and allowed (method, cost) pairs. Which choice, one that nobody offers, can the solver then make?

options.text: Aerial work by the own crew at $70k
options.says: The (method, who) table has no (aerial, own crew) row, so this pair is still refused.

options.text: Manual work by the contractor at $30k
options.says: The (method, who) table has no (manual, contractor) row, so this pair is still refused.

options.text: Manual work by the own crew at $40k
options.says: The (method, cost) table has no (manual, $40k) row, so this price is still refused.

options.text: Mechanical work by the contractor at $40k
options.says: Right: (mechanical, contractor) and (mechanical, $40k) are each allowed, and only a row naming all three ties a price to its provider.

questions.heading: Forbidden Pairs and a Flattened Element Price a Crew's Moves
questions.stem: A travel table T covers 6 places, numbered 0 to 5, and is flattened row by row (row: the place left) into a list of 36 costs. Which index reads the cost of a move from place a to place b?

options.says: Right: row a starts at entry 6a, and column b is b entries further on.
That is T[b][a], the move from b to a, which differs from T[a][b] as soon as the table is not symmetric.
The multiplier is the length of a row, the number of places, 6; with 5 the rows overlap.
Many moves share a sum (0 to 3, 1 to 2, 2 to 1, ...), so the index cannot tell them apart.
